newsitem.title: USA: Ribi says Melacine launch possible in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ribi says Melacine launch possible in 1997.

text.p: Ribi ImmunoChem Research Inc could launch its Melacine treatment for advanced melanoma as soon as this year if the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted its request for an accelerated review, the company's chief executive Officer said on Monday.

Speaking at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare Conference, the chief executive, Robert Ivy, said the company would also seek approval of Melacine in Canada in the first quarter of this year and in Europe in the second quarter.
Drug applications in Canada are automatically applied to the Australian market, where the incidence of melanoma is "very high," Ivy said.
Some 110,000 patients a year in the United States are diagnosed with stages three and four of melanoma, the advanced forms of the disease, which usually results in death in less than a year.

Ivy said Ribi was optimistic that the FDA would grant an accelerated review because of trials that showed Melacine produced a "very significant improvement" in survival rates compared with conventional chemotherapy treatments, he said.
The treatment was also shown to improve the ability of patients to function normally and cut adverse side effects of conventional chemotherapy by more than half, he said.
"Our pre-filing meetings with the FDA were very encouraging," Ivy said.
He added that Ribi was also looking at Melacine's potential in treating stage two melanoma, in which patients who have a tumor removed show a 30 percent rate of recurrence.
He said the final analysis of that data should be completed in October 1998.
"By the end of 1998 or early 1999, we should be taking a major share of the (melanoma market)," he said.
